memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The ancestral tribe of the Levites, however, was not counted along with the others. The Lord had said to Moses: "You must not count the tribe of Levi or include them in the census of the other Israelites." - Num 1:47-49 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One tribe stands apart from all the counting — the Levites. They were not numbered with the others because God had set them aside for a special purpose. While the other tribes prepared for battle and the ordinary duties of the nation, the Levites were dedicated to the service of God and His dwelling place.

This teaches us something precious: God sets people apart for Himself. The Levites were not better than the others, but they were given a holy calling — to care for the things of God. Being "set apart" was not about privilege but about devoted service.

Every believer today is, in a sense, set apart for God. The New Testament calls all who trust in Christ a "royal priesthood," a people belonging to God (1 Pet 2:9). We may not serve in a tabernacle, but we are called to live lives dedicated to Him — in our homes, our work, our worship, and our witness.

The Levites remind us that some things in life are meant to be devoted wholly to God, not tangled up with everything else. Our worship, our time, our hearts — these are set apart for Him.

Have you offered yourself to God as someone set apart for His service? You do not need a special title to live a dedicated life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean for you to be "set apart" for God?
- Are there parts of your life you have not yet devoted to Him?
- How can you live today as one belonging wholly to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, thank You for setting me apart for Yourself in Christ. Help me to live a dedicated life, giving my heart fully to You. Amen.
